 Grand Theft Auto 6 release sparks massive boom in Xbox and PlayStation 5 sales
 An estimated 2.8 million UK adults are expected to play the much-anticipated GTA VI on launch day alone
 Mike Taylor Wednesday 18 November 2026 11:36 EST

 Retailers report a sharp surge in sales of video game hardware as players prepare for the impending arrival of Grand Theft Auto VI. 
 Roughly 2.8 million adults across the UK are projected to play the highly anticipated title on launch day alone, following its midnight release on 19 November. 
 The excitement has prompted tens of thousands of employees to book time off, while certain companies are granting staff a holiday. Meanwhile, a school in Northern Ireland has reportedly issued a letter to parents warning that the release of GTA VI does not constitute a valid reason to skip lessons.
 Ahead of the launch, department store group John Lewis reported a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in console and accessory sales over the past three weeks compared with the same period last year.
 Calum Roscoe, computing and gaming buyer at John Lewis, said: "We’re seeing a real surge in customers preparing their setups ahead of the new Grand Theft Auto launch."
 He noted that consumers were not merely purchasing new hardware, but were "investing in the full setup" in anticipation of the title.
 Luke Starik plays Grand Theft Auto 6 as New Zealand is the first in the world to get access at midnight in Auckland ( AFP/Getty ) Online marketplace Gumtree stated that it has also recorded "growing interest" in gaming equipment as "excitement builds" among players ahead of the debut.
 Daily searches on the platform for PS5s are up 50 per cent this month compared with October, while searches for Xbox Series X are up 60 per cent and Xbox Series S are up 90 per cent.
 The excitement is not reserved to the UK, with many news outlets in Australia and the US also discussing a potential spike in sick days, coined as “GTA flu”.
 Japanese gaming company Pocketpair has offered its 98 employees up to five days of “special leave” starting from Thursday.
 A Pocketpair spokesperson told the Press Association: “We believe that playing and enjoying games is just as important as creating them.
 “Experiencing great games first-hand can inspire new ideas, spark creativity, and remind us why we love making games in the first place.
 “GTA VI is one of the most anticipated releases in the gaming industry, and we want our employees to have the opportunity to fully enjoy this special occasion without worrying about work.”
 It has also been reported that a brigade of soldiers in the US army have been offered days off to play the game, as long as they sign up for more service.
 According to US media outlets, 20 soldiers of the 3rd Infantry Division’s 9th Brigade Engineering Battalion have chosen to re-enlist after being presented with the opportunity for some off-time to play the new game.
